note: Pace is a MINIMUM with a 1 km floor; every other axis is a maximum. Ties keep the EARLIER row. `axisValues` is per row in the order [distance, duration, pace, calories]; null = cannot compete. Non-finite numbers in the input are serialised as null by JSON — Swift decodes them as absent, which is what the TS treats them as.

cases.name: runs — the faster 5k takes pace, the 8k takes distance and calories
the 8k row holds distance, duration and calories
walks — a tie on calories keeps the earlier row
the later walk wins pace and duration only
zero, missing and negative values do not compete
an unknown row id holds nothing
a single run holds every axis it can
